table_title: List selected major architectural styles spanning ancient through 20th-century traditions with global coverage (4 non-Western styles included for civilizational balance), with a curator-selected landmark building per style, the modern-day country where the landmark is located, and the year of completion.
db_analog: SELECT architectural_style, landmark_building, modern_day_country, year_of_completion FROM architectural_styles WHERE style_in_survey_canon_slate = TRUE ORDER BY architectural_style
temporal_note: Two Wikipedia master articles + 16 per-style + 16 per-building Wikipedia articles, accessed 2026-05-15. Universe is the 16 architectural styles commonly covered in survey-canon textbook treatments of the history of architecture, with global coverage including 4 non-Western styles (Mesoamerican, Japanese, Moorish, Mughal) per audit-recommended civilizational balance over a 12-row Western-only alternative. Per-row cells: Architectural Style is taken from the corresponding Wikipedia per-style article's canonical title (Ancient Egyptian architecture, Ancient Greek architecture, Ancient Roman architecture, Byzantine architecture, Romanesque architecture, Gothic architecture, Renaissance architecture, Baroque architecture, Neoclassical architecture, Art Nouveau, Art Deco, Modern architecture, Mesoamerican architecture, Japanese architecture, Moorish architecture, Mughal architecture). Landmark Building is curator-selected per the documented Landmark Rule from the per-style article's listed examples / textbook convention — single most-iconic example per style. Modern-day Country is the modern-day sovereign country of the landmark's site location per the per-building Wikipedia article (Hagia Sophia = Turkey not Byzantine; Pantheon = Italy not Roman Empire; etc.). Year of Completion is the integer year extracted from the per-building Wikipedia article's infobox 'Completed'/'Built' field where present OR from the article body's completion statement where the infobox uses a non-Completed field, with explicit exceptions documented for buildings with multi-phase or approximate completion: Great Pyramid of Giza -2600 (c. 2600 BC per standard chronology), Pyramid of the Sun 200 (c. 200 AD per article's Founded date), Versailles 1715 (largely-completed-by-Louis-XIV's-death per article's primary completion-period statement), Alhambra 1391 (Palace of the Lions / Nasrid-palace apogee under Muhammad V's second reign 1362-1391, latest year of range), Hōryū-ji 607 (infobox 'Completed 607' per article; the original burned 670 and current complex was probably completed around 711, but the staged year follows the infobox-priority default of the Year Rule). The 16-row universe is stable on a multi-year horizon: the textbook-canon architectural styles and their iconic landmark buildings have been canonical for decades to centuries.
_extraction_notes: Original instance SATURATING `qualitative` at 5/5 — SEVENTH CATEGORY TO FULLY CLEAR after multi_attribute_projection 8/8, set_operation 8/8, set_filter 5/5, causal 5/5, factual_lookup 6/5 over-target, top_k 6/5 over-target. Two rounds of pre-staging audit review preceded cycle-0 staging. Round 1 surfaced 5 design issues (universe scope overclaim 'major architectural styles', Year column not source-stable, per-style source plan missing, Country normalization, claim_type confirmation). Round 2 verified all 5 fixes applied and surfaced 3 additional pre-staging fixes (canonicalize Style PKs to Wikipedia article titles, Hōryū-ji year semantics, Alhambra year 1370 not source-verbatim). All 8 pre-staging issues addressed before any CSV/draft/curation files were written. Source plan: Tier B Wikipedia, source_count = 34 — 2 master (History of architecture, List of architectural styles) + 16 per-style + 16 per-building Wikipedia articles. Pipeline: (1) consult History_of_architecture for universe-context and period-by-style narrative; (2) consult List_of_architectural_styles for style-candidate enumeration including non-Western sections; (3) for each of 16 styles fetch the per-style Wikipedia article for canonical style name + landmark-building-examples; (4) for each of 16 landmark buildings fetch the per-building Wikipedia article for Modern-day Country + Year of Completion. Result: 16 rows × 4 columns, PK on Architectural Style, 0 duplicates. Civilizational distribution: 12 Western/Euro-Mediterranean (Ancient Egyptian + Greek + Roman + Byzantine + Romanesque + Gothic + Renaissance + Baroque + Neoclassical + Art Nouveau + Art Deco + Modern) + 4 non-Western (Mesoamerican + Japanese + Moorish + Mughal). Country distribution (11 distinct): France 3, Italy 2, Germany 2, Spain 2, singletons (Egypt, Greece, United States, Turkey, Japan, Mexico, India). Temporal span: -2600 BCE (Great Pyramid) to 1931 CE (Villa Savoye) — 4,531 year range. Confidence gradient: very-LLM-knowable cells include canonical iconic landmarks (Parthenon → Greece → -432; Pantheon → Italy → 126; Notre-Dame → France → 1345; Versailles → France → 1715; Chrysler Building → US → 1930; Taj Mahal → India → 1653); mid-difficulty cells include textbook-canonical extensions (Florence Cathedral → Italy → 1436; Brandenburg Gate → Germany → 1791; Speyer Cathedral → Germany → 1106; Casa Batlló → Spain → 1906; Villa Savoye → France → 1931); harder calibration cells include the non-Western and approximate-year rows (Hōryū-ji → Japan → 607 per infobox; Pyramid of the Sun → Mexico → 200 approximate; Alhambra → Spain → 1391 Palace-of-the-Lions apogee). The Landmark Building cell is the cell-type most likely to attract cycle-1 audit attention because it involves curator-judgment selection of a single most-iconic example per style; per-row landmark-selection rationale is documented in normalization_decisions for all 16 rows.
